newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank fx refinancing at $101 mln in H1.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank fx refinancing at $101 mln in H1.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) foreign currency refinancing to local commercial banks totalled $101.3 million in the first half of this year, the BNB said.
"Discount loans fell 25 percent to $51 million from January through June while foreign currency deposits rose 51.7 percent to $50.3 million," the BNB's semi-annual report said.
Central bank's discount loans and deposits in foreign currency in local commercial banks stood at $68.2 million and at $33.2 million respectively at the end of last year.
Deposits and discount loans were extended in U.S dollars and German marks at annual interest rates ranging between nine percent for discount loans and 6.5-8.0 percent for deposits.
Under BNB regulations its deposits in local banks are not considered a part of its foreign exchange reserves, which fell to $573.4 million at the end of June from $1.236 billion at the end of 1995.

Uncollateralised lev-denominated refinancing stood at 52.9 billion levs, of which 54.3 percent or 28.8 billion levs were distributed among three of the five banks, for which the central bank initiated bankruptcy procedures in May and June, the report said.

The BNB has opened bankruptcy procedures for state-owned Mineralbank and for First Private Bank (FPB), Krystalbank, Agrobusinessbank and Private Agricultural and Investment Bank (PAIB) since June due to a danger of insolvency.
"Some 92 percent of central bank lev-denominated refinancing in the first half were uncolateralised deposits, 6.8 percent were Lombard loans and 0.7 percent were discount loans," the report said.
The BNB lev-denominated refinancing totalled 57.6 billion levs by the end of June and was distributed among 12 of the 47 banks operating in the country.

BNB's foreign currency deposits and lev-denominated uncollateralised deposits in local commercial banks were considered very risky by an International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission, which has recommended the central bank to halt them by year's end.
